content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, the Sabbath is most commonly interpreted symbolically as a type or foreshadowing of the rest found in Christ and, ultimately, of God's eschatological rest — the believer ceasing from works-righteousness and entering salvation rest now, with a fuller eternal rest to come. The weekly Sabbath, rooted in God's rest at creation, is read as a 'shadow' whose substance is Christ.","primary_basis":["Genesis 2:2-3","Exodus 20:8-11","Deuteronomy 5:12-15","Hebrews 3:7-4:11 (especially 4:9-10, the 'sabbatismos' that remains for the people of God)","Matthew 11:28-30 ('Come to me... I will give you rest')","Colossians 2:16-17 (Sabbath as 'a shadow of things to come; the substance belongs to Christ')","Mark 2:27-28 / Matthew 12:8 ('The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath')"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Covenant sign and mark of sanctification: the Sabbath as a perpetual sign between God and his people, signifying that God sanctifies them; emphasized in Jewish interpretation and in covenantal Christian theology.","basis":["Exodus 31:12-17","Ezekiel 20:12, 20","Isaiah 58:13-14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Perpetual moral command still binding on the seventh day (Saturday), not merely symbolic: the Sabbath as an unabrogated creation ordinance and end-time test of loyalty (Seventh-day Adventist and other seventh-day Sabbatarian traditions).","basis":["Genesis 2:2-3","Exodus 20:8-11","Matthew 5:17-19","Luke 4:16","Revelation 14:7, 12 (as read by Adventists)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Transferred fulfillment in the Lord's Day (Sunday): the moral principle of one-day-in-seven rest and worship continues but is moved to the first day in honor of the resurrection (classic Reformed/Puritan Sabbatarianism; Westminster Confession).","basis":["Acts 20:7","1 Corinthians 16:2","Revelation 1:10","Exodus 20:8-11 (as abiding moral law)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Millennial or cosmic-week typology: six days of creation prefigure six thousand years of history, with the Sabbath symbolizing a coming seventh 'day' of millennial or eternal rest (patristic writers such as the Epistle of Barnabas, Irenaeus, Augustine's 'eternal sabbath').","basis":["Genesis 2:2-3","Psalm 90:4","2 Peter 3:8","Revelation 20:1-6 (as correlated by patristic exegesis)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Social-liberation and creation-care reading: Sabbath as a symbol of release from oppression, economic justice, and rest for land, workers, and creation, linked to sabbatical year and Jubilee (prominent in modern biblical theology, e.g., Brueggemann, Moltmann).","basis":["Deuteronomy 5:12-15","Exodus 23:10-12","Leviticus 25","Isaiah 61:1-2 with Luke 4:16-21"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a recognizable dominant consensus in Christian interpretation: the Sabbath symbolizes rest in Christ and anticipates eschatological rest, grounded chiefly in Hebrews 3-4 and Colossians 2:16-17. However, the practical/normative question (whether and how a Sabbath day remains binding) is genuinely contested across traditions (Adventist seventh-day observance, Reformed Sunday Sabbatarianism, and the majority 'fulfilled in Christ' view). These disputes concern application more than the core symbolic meaning of rest, which is broadly shared. Jewish interpretation (covenant sign, sanctification of time) also strongly informs the covenant-sign reading within Christian scholarship."}
